features.name: Professional tenure
features.description: This captures how much post-degree software engineering time the applicant presents, which signals likely maturity and depth of exposure.

levels.descriptor: Less than about 3 years or barely at minimum, with little sign of growing scope.
Around 3 years, showing credible early-career experience but limited seasoning.
Around 5 years, showing solid mid-career depth and sustained practice.
Around 7 or more years, or equivalent depth, suggesting seasoned ownership across multiple cycles.

features.name: Production shipping breadth
features.description: This captures how many real production systems the letter claims the applicant has tested, maintained, or launched.

levels.descriptor: Production scope is vague or very limited, with at most one clearly owned service.
The letter shows clear responsibility across about 2 production services.
The letter shows repeated production delivery across about 4 services.
The letter shows broad production breadth across 6 or more services or similarly wide operational scope.

features.name: Advanced academic training
features.description: This captures the highest level of formal academic training explicitly cited in the letter.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree or equivalent only, with no graduate study mentioned.
Master's degree or other clear graduate training is cited.
Doctoral training is cited.

features.name: Python production depth
features.description: This captures how strongly the letter establishes Python as a real production language rather than a casual scripting tool.

levels.descriptor: No meaningful Python experience is mentioned.
Python is mentioned briefly, but without clear production ownership or regular use.
Python is presented as a regular tool for services, automation, analysis, or internal tooling.
Python is presented as a core production language, with evidence such as typed or tested systems, internal platforms, or agent tooling others depend on.

features.evidence: "wrapped in the checks that make it dependable"
features.name: AI operational rigor
features.description: This captures whether AI experience is presented as production engineering with reliability controls rather than as a novelty claim.

levels.descriptor: No AI experience is mentioned.
AI is mentioned generically, with no evidence of deployment or operational care.
The letter cites shipped AI or LLM features in production.
The letter cites shipped AI systems plus explicit evaluation, hardening, guardrails, or failure-mode management.

features.name: Agentic control design
features.description: This captures how concretely the letter describes designing agentic tooling with bounded autonomy and supporting infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agentic tooling or agent design is mentioned.
Agents are mentioned, but only at a buzzword level without architecture or controls.
The letter describes agentic systems with a recognizable split such as Python agents plus Go services.
The letter explains how autonomy is constrained through contracts, permissions, auditability, or explicit guardrails, showing deliberate control design.

features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: This captures direct experience automating the intake, classification, routing, or deduplication of security reports.

levels.descriptor: No vulnerability-handling automation is mentioned.
The letter expresses interest in security automation, but gives no direct triage example.
The letter cites direct work automating triage, routing, or deduplication of vulnerability reports.
The letter shows clear ownership of triage automation and explains both mechanism and impact, such as reduced manual handling or returned expert time.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: This captures whether the applicant shows concrete experience evaluating systems for security risk, not just interest in security.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment work is described.
Security interest is implied, but assessment work is only vague or indirect.
The letter cites concrete assessment work such as threat modeling, code review, or service reviews.
The letter shows mature assessment practice, including findings, remediation follow-through, cross-stack scope, or an explicitly attacker-informed approach.

features.evidence: "make an intractable dedup problem boringly fast"
features.name: Data-structure fluency
features.description: This captures whether the letter demonstrates applied algorithmic judgment through concrete examples rather than generic claims.

levels.descriptor: No data-structure or algorithm evidence is provided.
The letter claims strong algorithms knowledge, but gives no real example.
The letter gives a concrete example of an algorithmic redesign or optimization.
The example shows strong production judgment, such as fixing a hot path, replacing a brute-force approach, or choosing structures that materially changed system behavior.

features.name: Security credentialing
features.description: This captures the strength of formal security certification explicitly cited in the letter.

levels.descriptor: No security certification is mentioned.
A foundational certification such as Security+ is cited.
A hands-on practical certification such as OSCP is cited.

features.name: Offensive practice
features.description: This captures whether the letter shows active effort to build an attacker's perspective through offensive security practice.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-security practice is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional CTF participation or a general attacker mindset.
The letter shows regular CTF participation or sustained offensive practice.
The letter shows especially strong offensive evidence, such as top placements, serious commitment, or a central role for offensive practice in the applicant's development.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: This captures whether the applicant shows responsibility for software beyond their employer through upstream contribution or maintenance.

levels.descriptor: No open-source work is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional patches or fixes sent upstream.
The letter shows regular contribution or maintainership, including review or release responsibilities.
The letter shows stewardship of a broadly used project or community, with clear responsibility for releases, roadmap, or contributor management.

features.evidence: "built a fault-tolerant message broker from scratch"
features.name: Independent systems building
features.description: This captures the technical ambition of personal projects used to demonstrate initiative beyond day-job work.

levels.descriptor: No independent project work is mentioned.
The letter mentions a small utility or simple side app with limited technical scope.
The letter shows a substantial personal project with clear end-to-end technical ownership.
The letter shows an ambitious independent systems project, especially distributed or infrastructure-heavy work with difficult edge cases.

features.evidence: "improvements there are inherited by every team downstream"
features.name: Platform leverage motivation
features.description: This captures how strongly the applicant is motivated by foundational infrastructure work whose impact multiplies across many teams.

levels.descriptor: Motivation is generic to the company or job title, with little platform-specific reasoning.
The letter mentions scale or impact in broad terms.
The letter clearly frames the role's appeal around foundational systems or organization-wide leverage.
The letter repeatedly and convincingly ties past choices and future goals to platform-level multiplicative impact.

features.evidence: "helping busy developer teams do the secure thing by default"
features.name: Developer enablement orientation
features.description: This captures whether the letter treats security engineering as making secure behavior easier for developers rather than as policing them.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not discuss developer users or workflow impact.
The letter says it wants to help teams, but without a clear enablement model.
The letter explicitly emphasizes removing friction or making the secure path the default.
The letter shows strong empathy for developer workflows and frames security tooling as capacity-building service design for internal users.

features.name: Maintainer mindset
features.description: This captures whether the applicant brings an operability and inheritability perspective shaped by testing, maintenance, or long-term ownership.

levels.descriptor: No maintainer or operator perspective is visible.
Testing or maintenance is listed as background, but not connected to design philosophy.
The letter explicitly links maintenance experience to reliability, operability, or design choices.
A strong inheritability philosophy runs through the letter, showing that the applicant designs for the people who will operate or inherit the system later.

features.name: Impact articulation
features.description: This captures how well the letter explains the effect of the applicant's work rather than just naming tasks or technologies.

levels.descriptor: The letter mostly lists responsibilities, tools, or interests without clear results.
The letter gives examples of work, but the consequences remain abstract.
The letter describes tangible effects such as time saved, bugs removed, or manual work reduced.
The letter gives vivid or quantified leverage that makes the applicant's impact especially credible and easy to picture.

features.name: Copy accuracy
features.description: This captures how free the letter is from visible typos, misspellings, and other surface errors that affect credibility.

levels.descriptor: Frequent visible errors distract from the content and materially weaken the presentation.
Several errors appear, but the letter remains readable overall.
Only occasional minor errors appear.
The letter is clean or nearly clean at the surface level.

features.name: Security worldview
features.description: This captures whether the letter expresses a thoughtful model of what good security engineering is for and how it should operate.

levels.descriptor: No real security viewpoint is articulated beyond general interest.
The letter states that security matters, but the philosophy is thin or generic.
The letter presents a clear viewpoint, such as proactive assistance, quiet resilience, or defaults over policy.
The letter offers a nuanced security philosophy that is clearly tied to the applicant's engineering choices and the role's mission.

features.evidence: "I started my career on the unglamorous side of software"
features.name: Narrative distinctiveness
features.description: This captures how memorable and well-shaped the letter's overall voice and framing are.

levels.descriptor: The letter feels interchangeable, checklist-driven, or heavily templated.
The letter has some personal framing, but is still mostly standard and forgettable.
The letter has a noticeable voice or framing device that helps the applicant stand out.
The letter delivers a vivid, controlled narrative that is both memorable and well matched to the role.
